what: REFUTED EXEMPLAR, found reading Bram Stoker's Dracula (Project Gutenberg #345) in full for the first time under the composition-omitted-activation fix (III.4): the-fold/hypergraph.js::resolvePronounSubjects rewrites a pronoun subject to its resolved referent's own surface, then makeRelationReader re-runs spans.js::splitSentences on the REWRITTEN text and pairs the resulting sentence count against the count from the ORIGINAL text. At small excerpt windows (8000-48000 chars) this pairing holds. At full-book scale (845,931 chars, 1,514 real pronoun bindings applied), it does not: original sentence count 9470, rewritten sentence count 9770 — a divergence of 300, because many resolved referent surfaces in a Victorian novel carry title abbreviations (Dr., Mrs., Mr.) whose periods a naive splitter reads as new sentence boundaries the author never wrote. Because the pairing check is PASSAGE-SCOPED (one boolean for the whole document, not per-sentence), a SINGLE such divergence anywhere in the book zeroes the span on every one of the 15,149 extracted edges at once — the reading gates gapped_self_verify with zero admitted notes, having genuinely extracted real content the whole time.

reproduction.file: the-fold/hypergraph.js::resolvePronounSubjects, makeRelationReader's own extractionList/list sentence-count pairing check
reproduction.input: live_priors/01-literature-books/gutenberg/pg345_Dracula.txt, full text (845,931 chars post-container-strip and newline-normalisation)
reproduction.measured: 1514 pronoun bindings, 0 refused as stale (offsets consistent with the already-normalised excerpt, unlike the CRLF-drift case measured separately on Hamlet); 1514 substitutions applied; original sentence count 9470; rewritten sentence count 9770; paired=false for the whole passage
reproduction.consequence: makeRelationReader's own comment states the design intent correctly ('a wrong address is worse than a coarse one') and the wall IS working as designed — refusing every span it cannot trust rather than guessing one. The defect is upstream: the pairing check tests the WRONG invariant. Two independently-derived sentence counts over two DIFFERENT texts (one the author wrote, one this instrument wrote) were never guaranteed to agree, and testing whether they happen to is a symptom, not a safeguard.

root_cause: A category error, corrected mid-conversation by direct user pushback (2026-09-01): the FIRST design fix proposed treating segmentation-on-the-untouched-bytes as a fixed oracle never to be re-derived. That is necessary but insufficient. Segmentation is itself a claim — a SEG·Figure act, exactly the shape every other entry in this project's own append-only logs already takes — and even a first pass against real, unmutated bytes is a HEURISTIC (a splitter can misjudge 'Dr. Seward met Mr. Harker' with no rewrite involved at all). The correct standing, stated by the user directly: 'what if the first assertion of punctuation is wrong? we have a whole intelligence of search and seek and stuff. and yes its all append only.'
not_yet_done: no fix landed in this pass. Two things named, neither built: (1) a pronoun binding should be handed to endpoint()/noteIdentity as an identity claim about an ALREADY-fixed span — never used to rewrite the string and re-split the document; (2) if a later reading proposes a DIFFERENT segmentation of a passage than the one already on record, that proposal is itself a claim, checked by the SAME apparatus every other claim in this system answers to before it lands (grid.js's EVA/concedeEvaluation, refutation.js's veto on genuine incoherence, seek.js's evidence-driven navigation) — landed as a witnessed SUPERSEDE/REC on the append-only log, never a silent recomputation whose only check is whether a sentence COUNT happened to match.
status: PARTIALLY CLOSED, 2026-09-01, same pass: hypergraph.js's resolvePronounSubjects was replaced with pronounBindingsFor + sentenceWithPronouns (per-sentence-local substitution, never a whole-passage rewrite), closing the sentence-count-drift mechanism this finding names. NOT yet closed: causal ordering of WHICH surface a pronoun substitutes — segmentation.js (new, this pass) provides the cursor-stamped, append-only PROPOSE/SUPERSEDE/REC vocabulary for a forward-only first pass plus an explicitly-dated later correction, matching LP2's Talmud framing and user direction ('a reading later can always CHANGE our past reading... yes its all append only'); wiring it into hypergraph.js's own pronoun-binding selection is the next integration step, not completed in this pass.
